name: A game's start function cleans up after itself
instruction: The function returned by a CarnivalGame's start cancels its animation frame and removes every listener that start added.
relevant_when: A game's game.ts file under src/games/<game-id>/ whose start function calls addEventListener, requestAnimationFrame, setTimeout or setInterval.
context: AGENTS.md house rule 5. The midway starts and stops games as people walk between booths, so a listener or frame left behind keeps running against a game that is gone. Review of the rollercoaster (PR #2) also found input that could stay latched when a release never arrived.
scope_reason: start and the cleanup function it returns are in the same file, so every add and remove can be matched by reading it.

checklist.name: listeners-removed
checklist.rule: For every addEventListener call made in start, the returned cleanup function calls removeEventListener on the same target, with the same event type and the same handler reference.

checklist.name: frames-and-timers-cancelled
checklist.rule: If start calls requestAnimationFrame, the cleanup calls cancelAnimationFrame with the latest frame id; if start calls setTimeout or setInterval, the cleanup clears them. Not applicable when start schedules none of these.
